data.title: Lichen simplex chronicus — viva
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Lichen simplex chronicus** (Eczemas)_

**Q1. Define LSC.**
- Localised lichenified plaque resulting from repeated rubbing/scratching (itch–scratch cycle) without a primary dermatosis (or superimposed on one)

**Q2. Common sites?**
- Nape of neck (women), ankles/shins, scrotum/vulva, wrists, extensor forearms, scalp (occipital), upper eyelids

**Q3. Clinical features?**
- Well-defined thickened plaque with exaggerated skin markings, hyperpigmentation, excoriations; paroxysmal intense itch, often at night or with stress

**Q4. Associated factors?**
- Anxiety, depression, obsessive-compulsive traits, atopy, xerosis, underlying contact dermatitis, insect bites, neuropathic itch

**Q5. Differential diagnosis?**
- Lichen planus (hypertrophic), psoriasis, tinea (KOH), lichen amyloidosis, chronic contact dermatitis, nummular eczema, mycosis fungoides, prurigo nodularis

**Q6. Histopathology?**
- Compact orthohyperkeratosis, irregular psoriasiform acanthosis, hypergranulosis, vertically streaked collagen in papillary dermis

**Q7. Treatment?**
- Break itch–scratch cycle: potent topical steroids under occlusion, intralesional triamcinolone, occlusive dressings (prevent scratching), topical calcineurin inhibitors, capsaicin, doxepin
- Antihistamines (sedating at night), SSRIs/anxiolytics, behavioural therapy; treat underlying cause

## Quick spotter facts
- Thick lichenified plaque on the nape of the neck — lichen simplex chronicus

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Lichen simplex chronicus); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.24 and ch.72. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
